Independent diagonal-majorant/equality certificate and exact three-node inverse
correctness.rationale: With times 0,…,N the phase-free frame matrix is DCD for D=diag(|g_i|). C=VVᵀ with V_ik=a_i^k. For each minor, the Cauchy–Binet terms are products of positive generalized Vandermonde determinants (ordinary Vandermonde on the ordered positive nodes times a Schur polynomial with nonnegative coefficients and at least one positive monomial). N+1≥n ensures nonempty sums. Cofactors give the strict checkerboard sign of C⁻¹, hence H>0 entrywise. For an independent certificate, let p_i=|g_i|² and t>0. When p has full support, W≥tI iff diag(p)≥tH by inversion, congruence and the checkerboard signature. If any p_i vanishes, the smallest eigenvalue is zero. The all-ones test gives t≤1/L. The proposed p attains it because diag(r)−H is the positive semidefinite weighted graph Laplacian with quadratic form (1/2)∑ H_ij|x_i−x_j|². Equality forces (diag(p)−tH)1=0, so exactly p=r/L; phases are immaterial. In the three-mode example, the columns of V⁻¹ are coefficients of 8x²−10x+3, −16x²+16x−3 and 8x²−6x+1; applying the checkerboard signs to their coefficient Gram gives the displayed H and L=2097. When the horizon is shorter the rank is at most N+1; when two modes coincide their projected orbit spans at most one direction. Both listed degeneracies give zero.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns unconstrained complex phases and one sensor, positive distinct real modal eigenvalues and consecutive finite observations. It does not guarantee numerically stable inversion for ill-conditioned C.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These are strong method and statement overlaps. An asymptotic small-horizon theorem does not provide an exact global finite rule.

originality.rationale: Pass for the exact discrete finite-horizon E-optimal allocation, including uniqueness and validity at every admissible horizon. The row-sum form and its sign argument are not new as general design ideas: Chen–Belabbas explicitly have the exact analogous law for the infinite continuous-time Cauchy kernel, and the same-day finite continuous-time result deploys essentially the same argument for an exponential integral kernel. Neither inspected statement contains the finite discrete kernel. The remaining distinct content is the exact allocation for every consecutive finite discrete horizon and the needed strict inverse-sign proof for that family, not a new general optimization principle.
residual_risks: The structural overlap with the same-day continuous-window theorem and older continuous infinite-window law is substantial. An older general exact diagonal-majorant/scaling lemma combined with an applicable total-positivity theorem, or an equivalent discrete-time control statement, may provide additional prior coverage. Bounded review does not certify historical priority.

value.rationale: Finite consecutive observations under a unit-energy constraint are a natural sensor-design problem. The exact worst-mode bound and unique amplitude allocation give a horizon-specific benchmark down to the minimum number of observations without performing a sensor optimization. A continuous integral or infinite-time limit need not give the same amplitudes for the actual discrete horizon; the inverse-sign certificate explains why an exact simple law still works there.
residual_risks: Value is for the exact discrete setting, not a new general actuator-design theory or a claim about conditioning of the numerical inversion.
